chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: What the snare seizes from the game, such that it cuts off its foreleg or hindleg — then leave it, for it is dead carrion. And eat what you find while it is still alive, having mentioned the Name of God, Mighty and Majestic, over it.

key_terms.الحِبَالَة: Snare or rope-trap used for catching game; distinct from projectile weapons
key_terms.ذَكَرْتُمُ اسْمَ اللَّهِ: Mentioning the name of God — the required basmala at the time of slaughter
key_terms.مَيِّت: Dead; legally deceased carrion (mayta), forbidden to consume

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game caught in a snare that severs a limb?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmits a ruling of Imam Ali (AS) regarding game caught in a snare or trap: if the trap severs a limb from the animal, the animal is considered legally dead (mayta) and therefore forbidden to eat. The permissible case is when the hunter reaches the animal while it is still alive and properly slaughters it with the basmala. This addresses a situation common among early Arabian hunters using rope-traps and snares for catching gazelles and birds — the ruling turns on whether the animal was killed by the trap itself (forbidden) or by proper ritual slaughter after capture (permitted).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What the snare seizes from the hunt, so a hand or a leg is cut off from it, so leave it, for it is dead, and eat from what you come to as alive, and you have mentioned the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said,
’If a prey is caught by a snare, whatever is cut off like a leg or so, must be thrown away; it is dead. You can use the rest that you find alive and the name of Allah was mentioned on it.’”
